question_record.context: A security incident involving malware detection and lateral movement attempt was reported. An active 'Kekeo' malware was detected running on the host `vnevado-win10b`, which was identified with the file `rubeus.exe` linked to the account `fk8mq` (SID: S-1-5-21-1540151660-3530000288-105586595-1517, AadUserId: 97e6a954-b6bd-48a5-808c-bd8464cce677). This was followed by an alert indicating that a file was dropped and launched from a remote location, potentially by an attacker or malware attempting to move laterally or propagate.
question_record.question: Who is the account associated with the file that was dropped and launched from a remote location in this incident?
solution: An active 'Kekeo' malware was detected on the host with AadDeviceId `fafdcd65-46c6-45a6-aa85-ec9b77ca0bcb`.
A file named `psexesvc.exe` was dropped and launched during a remote session.
The file was dropped and launched from an account with the name `lucasb`.

106.name: An active 'Kekeo' malware was detected
106.description:
Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

A malware is considered active if it is found running on the machine or it already has persistence mechanisms in place. Active malware detections are assigned higher severity ratings.

Because this malware was active, take precautionary measures and check for residual signs of infection.
